accepted.question_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional Banach space over a non-Archimedean valued field. Call a nonzero subspace E₁ of E prime if there is no proper subspace E₂ of E such that E is the orthogonal direct sum of E₁ and E₂. Every finite-dimensional Banach space can be decomposed as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces. Is this prime decomposition unique in a natural sense?
accepted.context_brief: Prime decompositions in non-Archimedean Banach spaces

evidence.quote: A non-zero subspace \(E\_ 1\) of a Banach space \(E\) is said to be prime if there is no proper subspace \(E\_ 2\) of \(E\) such that \(E\) is the orthogonal direct sum of \(E\_ 1\) and \(E\_ 2\). Every finite-dimensional Banach space can be decomposed as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces. Is the prime decomposition unique in a natural sense?

accepted.question_text: A p-adic normed space is called Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace has an orthogonal complement. Is every cartesian normed space Hilbertian?

evidence.quote: A \(p\)-adic normed space is called Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace has an orthogonal complement. The authors state that it is not known whether every cartesian normed space is Hilbertian.
One of the problems posed in this paper is the following: Is \(\ell^ 1\)- ultrametrizable?
This has been solved by J. M. Bayod negatively when the base field is non-trivially valued, and this has appeared in the same volume in which this paper under review has appeared.
